newsitem.title: USA: Accountant pleads guilty to securities, bank fraud.
newsitem.headline: Accountant pleads guilty to securities, bank fraud.

text.p: A Los Angeles accountant pleaded guilty to federal charges Wednesday that he conspired to defraud a bank and investors of three companies by inflating the firms' value, regulators said.

Merle Finkel, 66, entered his plea in U.S. District Court in Las Vegas to one count of conspiracy to commit bank fraud and securities fraud, the Justice Department said in a statement issued in Washington. He faces a maximum prison sentence of five years.

Finkel created false audited financial reports between August 1992 and January 1995 on behalf of Twenty-First Century Health Inc. as well as EMS Products International Corp. and Combined Companies International Corp. which later merged, the government said.

The government alleged that Finkel conspired with Las Vegas stock promoters and a Las Vegas businesswoman, among others, to create the false reports which inflated the true amount of the assets of the companies based in Las Vegas.
While it did not name the co-conspirators, the government said its investigation into the case was continuing.
The conspirators also created false personal financial statements and documents purported to be copies of federal income tax returns, the government said.

The false tax returns were designed to inflate the income and assets of Finkel's co-conspirators, who were officers or persons affiliated with the companies and were applying for loans at certain Las Vegas financial institutions, including First Security Bank, prosecutors said.

In a companion suit, Finkel, without admitting or denying the allegations, settled civil charges filed by the Securities and Exchange Commission that he violated federal securities laws in connection with filing false or inaccurate audit reports on three publicly traded companies.

As part of the settlement in U.S. District Court in Washington, Finkel agreed to be barred from appearing or practicing before the commission as a certified public accountant, the regulatory agency said.
The SEC said Finkel prepared inflated financial statements for Twenty-First Century Health, Combined Companies International and Systems of Excellence Inc.
Nasdaq Bulletin Board trading in shares of Twenty-First Century Health and Systems of Excellence has been suspended, it added.

In a related case, Charles Huttoe, former chairman and chief executive officer of Systems of Excellence was sentenced on Jan. 31 for his role in massive market manipulation involving the shares of the company.
He received 46 months in a federal prison followed by a two-year supervised release and a $10,000 fine.
Huttoe manipulated the market by using a stock promotor to falsely issue favorable information about his company and then selling shares after its price artifically rose.
